DESIGN PROTOTYPE
Implementation status · edition 09

Four CockroachDB stores and a local HTTP gateway form the container lab. Regional production gateways, HA, CDC/Kafka and distributed resource isolation are target designs. Check the implementation matrix before engineering from this page.

Legal entity federation / Design edition 04

Entity sovereignty, physical placement.

Separate the business federation boundary from the database deployment boundary.

New · executable entity relocation

Add Mumbai and move a synthetic India entity through copy, catch-up, validation, authority cutover and cleanup. Read the migration design · Open the monitor. This isolated slice complements the original three-store examples; normalized-table migration is an extension point.

Operational isolation decision · edition 07

Policy guard, operational delivery and bulk reconciliation have separate resource budgets. Policy activation performs bounded authority work; broad data movement runs independently. Read the revised contract · Run the isolation model. The v3 runtime remains a thin serial harness.

Operational model extension · v3

The working example now separates global party minimums from relationship graphs, with table defaults and major-key restrictions. Business model · Parallel controls · Service transactions. Earlier flat-record examples below remain illustrative; they do not define the normalized relationship key.

Logical model

LayerKey / contractMeaning
Identityglobal_customer_idOpaque identity; not permission to replicate a universal directory.
Ownershipowner_entity_id + global_customer_idIndependent customer relationship, authority and policy per legal entity.
Projectionowner + customer + destination_entity_idNo overwriting of another owner or recipient, even within the same store.
Placemententity_id → store_id + placement_versionPhysical host selected independently of incorporation and business grouping.
Geographystore.countryThe actual country evaluated against all applicable restrictions.

Deployment topology

PlanePoC deploymentProduction extension
ControlVersioned static entity/store directory and synthetic global monitorApproved regional metadata views, signed configuration and change governance.
BusinessOne local FastAPI harness containing entity-aware adaptersSame service image deployed near each approved store; authenticated regional gateways.
StorageSG, GB and US independent CockroachDB single nodesMultiple local failure domains at every physical store where HA is required.
FederationOwner outbox → source OPA → recipient OPA → scoped projectionRegional transport, distributed fences, signed permits and isolated credentials.
EvidenceRegional audit tables plus OTel SDK/Collector wiringApproved regional telemetry, immutable audit and retention controls.

One transaction boundary per authoritative store

Domains belonging to the same owner entity may share an in-process business transaction where that matches business invariants. Cross-entity operations require explicit authorisation even when rows share a database. Cross-store projections remain asynchronous. Physical co-location is neither an entitlement nor an instruction to consolidate all entity transactions.

Data flow and sequence

Denied candidates remain source-side decisions. No recipient call or customer-keyed destination artefact is created for a never-authorised route. Source and recipient use separate OPA processes; the diagram groups them for readability.

Implementation status: three nodes, thirty entities

The hosted experience is a browser simulation. The downloadable PoC uses real CockroachDB and OPA, but database end-to-end execution is not verified in this environment. Three logical locations on a laptop do not demonstrate physical geographic residency or HA. Production enforcement requires authenticated regional services and approved infrastructure.

Entity relocation decision: keep legal entity identity stable while changing physical home. Use a lawful transition policy, snapshot plus continuous change capture, versioned tombstones, target-applied checkpoints, graph closure and an entity-specific source writer fence. Persist source fencing before activating the target; never flip routing back after target writes. Separate placement version, writer epoch, policy revision and resource data version. Migration consumes the capped bulk lane; guard and operational capacity remain reserved. The executable edition-08 slice uses isolated mig_* row envelopes and one coordinator; it does not migrate the original normalized business.* fixture or prove distributed fencing. Read Entity relocation before implementation.

Operational isolation decision: use three regional work classes: authority guard, operational delivery and bulk reconciliation. Separate relay paths, queues/topics, worker groups, connection/concurrency budgets and retry/quarantine paths. A policy transaction advances scoped authority and creates a guard intent plus one reconciliation cursor; it must not enumerate affected rows. Operational commits remain local ACID with outbox/audit/idempotency. Operational priority never bypasses current policy. Source restriction commit, remote enforcement and physical convergence are separate milestones. Read the Work isolation page before implementing any queue or policy change. The interactive lab and admission specification are synthetic; the v3 database harness still has its original process lock and serial worker.

Extend the v3 operational PoC, preserving 30 legal entities and three independent single-node store models. Business data is normalized across 12 tables; sovereignty policies live in parallel control tables. A separate party scope exports only id/global_party_id/party_type; relationship scopes export connected whitelisted graphs. Global distribution still needs grants and approved geography; deny overrides. Do not infer relationship access from a global party, common store or shared identity. Keep the single local transaction and asynchronous destination acknowledgement distinct. The hosted UI is a labelled browser simulation. The unified Docker/CockroachDB/OPA suite and live Chromium generator/migration walkthrough passed. Database crash boundaries, accessibility and pilot load remain separate gates. Use synthetic data only. Deliver bounded adapters, actual migrations, meaningful invariant tests and honest run results.

Apply the normalized operational extension before the earlier component requirements below.

Design edition 04: 30 synthetic bank legal entities (UK 3, Asia 8, Americas 3, MENAT 5, rest of Europe 11), mapped independently to three physical PoC stores in Singapore, London and New York. Asia assumes one entity in each of eight countries. All names, mappings and country rules are illustrative, not legal advice or bank policy. Preserve global customer identity; master key is (owner_entity_id, global_customer_id); projection key additionally includes destination_entity_id. Sharing a store or global ID does not share entitlements. OPA evaluates entity grants AND resolved physical country restrictions, with deny override. The downloadable implementation is a single Python/FastAPI harness, three independent CockroachDB single nodes, three OPA engines, outbox polling and OpenTelemetry. The hosted monitor is a labelled browser simulation. Local HA, Java regional services, CDC/Kafka, distributed fencing and signed permits are production extension work. The original v3 catalog planner does not execute migrations. Edition 08 adds an isolated executable relocation slice and optional fourth store; see Entity relocation. Automatic geography failover remains prohibited.

Create deployment contracts for 30 entities and three physical store adapters. Keep the directory separate from customer facts. Prove LE-GB-02 can receive a projection while LE-GB-03 is denied on the same node. Add a topology inventory for SQL, queues, backup, telemetry and key custody; specify which boundaries are only simulated in Compose.
